source_context:
Furstenberg's evenly spaced topology on the integers, the vehicle of his 1955 topological proof of the infinitude of primes. The module defines the two-sided arithmetic progression {x | b dvd x - a} and the topology generated by the progressions with nonzero step, and proves the structural facts driving the argument: the progressions form a topological basis (with no gcd needed, since inside an intersection the progression with step b1*b2 through the common point suffices); each progression with nonzero step is clopen, its complement being the union of the progressions shifted by the nonzero residues; each progression is infinite, hence every nonempty open set is infinite; the covering identity that the progressions p*Z over all primes cover exactly Z minus {1, -1}; and the finiteness engine: any set of nonzero naturals whose progressions achieve that covering is infinite, since a finite union of closed progressions would be closed, making {1, -1} a finite nonempty open set. Composing the last two statements is precisely Furstenberg's proof. The composed conclusion, the infinitude of primes, is deliberately NOT restated: it exists in Mathlib as Nat.infinite_setOf_prime, and restating it would be an exact baseline duplicate. The mathematics is classical (Furstenberg 1955) and is not claimed as new; what is new to the tree is the topology and its structural theorems.

Absence evidence over the pinned Mathlib tree at v4.33.0-rc1. The string furstenberg has zero case-insensitive hits in Mathlib. No evenly spaced or profinite-style topology on Z generated by arithmetic progressions exists anywhere: Mathlib's topologies on Z are the order topology and instances derived from it. Mathlib proves the infinitude of primes by Euclid-style arguments (Nat.exists_infinite_primes) with no topological route. In the LeanFrontier corpus the Topology subject directory was previously empty.

Implementation. The topology is a plain definition, not an instance, so Z keeps its standard topology elsewhere; statements name it through Mathlib's scoped notation IsOpen[t] and IsClosed[t], and proofs bring it into instance scope with letI, shadowing the ambient instTopologicalSpaceInt. Closedness reduces to positive step via abs_dvd; the complement identity is exhibited with Int.emod_add_ediv_mul and closed by linarith, with divisibility of the residue excluded by Int.le_of_dvd. Infinitude of a progression embeds Z by k maps-to a + b*k using Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem. The covering identity uses Int.exists_prime_and_dvd and Int.prime_iff_natAbs_prime. Imports are three files: Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic, Mathlib.RingTheory.Int.Basic, Mathlib.Topology.Bases.

Verification beyond the receiver. The membership semantics of the progression definition were checked by decide on concrete instances (7 and -5 lie in the progression through 1 with step 3, 8 does not), and the covering identity was checked semantically on the window [-20, 20] against the primes up to 19 in a scratch computation outside the repository: an integer there is divisible by one of them exactly when it is not 1 or -1.

Not included. The infinitude of primes itself (an exact Mathlib duplicate, as noted); metrizability of the topology and its identification with the profinite metric; total disconnectedness; and Dirichlet-type refinements. Each of the last three is a genuine further result deserving its own submission.

Provenance. Produced by the same agent session as the four previous submissions of this series, from the repository's TRY-LEANFRONTIER launcher, after the human operator asked for a fifth submission without choosing a subject: the subject, absence check, statements, proofs, and the decision to submit were made by the agent. Proofs use structure construction, letI instance management, dvd algebra, one emod/ediv computation, linarith, and the named Mathlib lemmas above.
